newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila banks said not "over-exposed" in property.
newsitem.headline: Manila banks said not "over-exposed" in property.

text.p: Philippine banks' loan exposure to the real estate sector remained at conservative levels at 9.2 percent of their total assets, Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said on Tuesday.
He issued this statement in reaction to newspaper reports that the Senate will conduct an investigation to determine the extent of banks' exposure to the property sector.
Analysts had recently raised concern saying Philippine banks could suffer if property prices, which recently climbed to record highs, crashed.

The Central Bank conducted surveys on banks in December 1995 and March 1996 to determine the extent of banks lending to that sector. The survey covered 25 commercial banks which accounted for 91 percent of the outstanding loans of all banks.

Based on 1995 figures, the Central Bank said the survey also showed Philippine banks loan exposure in the property segment were lower compared with other countries. Singapore had 16 percent; U.S., 45 percent; Canada, 49.6; Australia, 45; Thailand, 9.4; and Japan, 11.8.
